### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/setup`, `@objectstack/studio`, `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **14** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **6** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/apps/setup/tsconfig.json`, `packages/apps/setup/vitest.config.ts`, `packages/apps/studio/tsconfig.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**14** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/ai/connect-mcp.mdx`  _(via setup.access (literal, a string literal in BookAudienceSchema))_
- `content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx`  _(via setup.access (literal, a string literal in BookAudienceSchema))_

- `content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx`  _(via crm_admin (literal, a string literal in a comment in BookAudienceSchema))_
- `content/docs/permissions/capabilities.mdx`  _(via setup.access (literal, a string literal in BookAudienceSchema))_
- `content/docs/permissions/delegated-administration.mdx`  _(via setup.access (literal, a string literal in BookAudienceSchema))_

⛔ **4** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v13.mdx`  _(via crm_admin (literal, a string literal in a comment in BookAudienceSchema))_
- `content/docs/releases/v14.mdx`  _(via crm_admin (literal, a string literal in a comment in BookAudienceSchema))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **6** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/apps/setup/tsconfig.json`, `packages/apps/setup/vitest.config.ts`, `packages/apps/studio/tsconfig.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **10** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **177** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 29e0c4bf5f6ca597b9d94a6c987db2a0cf6f7a8b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d645b0b557090a2d1213c054ed6a3c90c2c75c6c` — the merge of head `dc85e540745a89771114cb8810b27dcab6d9ee55` into base `29e0c4bf5f6ca597b9d94a6c987db2a0cf6f7a8b`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d645b0b557090a2d1213c054ed6a3c90c2c75c6c && git checkout d645b0b557090a2d1213c054ed6a3c90c2c75c6c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 29e0c4bf5f6ca597b9d94a6c987db2a0cf6f7a8b dc85e540745a89771114cb8810b27dcab6d9ee55 && git checkout -B drift-repro 29e0c4bf5f6ca597b9d94a6c987db2a0cf6f7a8b && git merge --no-ff dc85e540745a89771114cb8810b27dcab6d9ee55

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 29e0c4bf5f6ca597b9d94a6c987db2a0cf6f7a8b
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 29e0c4bf5f6ca597b9d94a6c987db2a0cf6f7a8b` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

**Test Core (4/10) on head `b9998850`: one timeout outside this PR.**

- Failing test: `packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-11389-date-tz-skew.test.ts:80`, "sweeps a zone EAST of UTC, a zone WEST of UTC, and UTC itself". It hit vitest's 5000 ms default after 5258 ms.
- The same shard was slow throughout: `import 973.90s`, a 378 s run. The other 4568 driver-sql tests passed.
- This PR changes no file under `packages/drivers/`. Its diff is spec book schema, lint, the setup and studio apps, docs and changesets, and none of them reach the driver's zone sweep.
- Nothing is pushed for it. A re-run of the shard should clear it.

The other red, **Check Changeset**, is the DELIBERATE CORRECTION of `.changeset/36029-book-audience-system-permission.md` already declared in the PR body.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b999885037f1d3707568389158b4476c6904fc59`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/19.book-audience-two-gates-and-catch-all-claim-refused.ts, packages/spec/src/system/book.zod.ts + packages/lint/src/validate-book-audience-claims.ts, packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts, packages/lint/src/index.ts

Read: card #37613 with its five comments (claim 7212725896, amendment 7214987476), the PR body and file list, the net diff against `main`, and the check-runs on this head. Cited code read on `main`, not reviewed: `shared/union-branch-policy.ts`, `shared/strict-object.ts`, `shared/retired-key.ts`, `migrations/types.ts`, `packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.ts`, `packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts`, ADR-0046 §6.7. The rest of the diff (the two `manual-claims-docs.test.ts` pins and their wiring, the rule's test, `book.test.ts`, the liveness row, generated `book.mdx`, docs pages) is the lane seat's ACCEPT.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept-set of `BookAudienceSchema`: narrowed by one shape, right.** Refused now and accepted before: an object with a string `permissionSet` and an own `systemPermission` key holding anything but `undefined` (a string, `null`, `''`), with or without other stray keys. Before, the set arm stripped the key. Nothing else moves: `{ permissionSet, label }` still parses and strips `label`; `{ permissionSet, systemPermission: undefined }` still parses; the `{ systemPermission }` arm refused every extra key already, and `strictObject` in place of `.strict()` changes its message only.
- **The prescription reaches the author on both key orders, right.** Read against `selectUnionBranches`: each object arm reports one issue, the strict arm carries `unrecognized_keys` and wins the tie, so the rendered line is the strict arm's with `BOOK_AUDIENCE_ONE_GATE` as its guidance. When the strict arm reports two issues (a non-string `systemPermission`), the set arm wins and prints the same sentence at `audience.systemPermission`. The wire mapper shares the selection.
- **Public surface of `@objectstack/spec`: no export added or removed.** `BOOK_AUDIENCE_ONE_GATE` is module-private. The set arm's JSON schema gains `systemPermission` as an unsatisfiable property and the generated reference shows it as `never`, the shape `retiredKey` tombstones already emit. The hand-written `BookAudience` type is unchanged.
- **Parsed output: one edge, harmless.** An audience written with an explicit `systemPermission: undefined` keeps that key in the parsed value (zod keeps a present optional key). Every reader in the tree tests `typeof ... === 'string'` (`audienceAllows`, `anyPermissionSetAudience`, `anySystemPermissionAudience`, the lint `gateOf`, `BookPreview`), so no gate reads it as a second form.
- **`@objectstack/lint`: one new exported rule and one new error id, right.** `book-gated-catch-all-include` is `gating` on `validate`, `build` and `lint`, and on the runtime publish gate for `book` writes. It is a new refusal of a shape 18.x accepted (a `{ permissionSet }` book claiming by `'*'`), declared as such in the changeset with FROM → TO.
- **Stored rows, right as stated.** The docs read gate lists stored books without parsing them and `audienceAllows` reads `permissionSet` first, so a stored two-gate row keeps the set gate it has today. On an update, the runtime gate drops the written item's stored self from the baseline, so the catch-all finding on the book being saved is charged, not cancelled: "the next save is refused" holds for both refusals.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: yes (narrowing) — on the PR body and on `.changeset/37613-book-audience-one-gate.md`, with `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` on both. Right: the diff changes a published schema's accept-set downward, and the claim's `no` / `none` was replaced by amendment 7214987476.

- `@objectstack/spec` minor and `@objectstack/lint` minor match the rule (a `narrowed` kind takes at least `minor` on each package the diff moves; BREAKING ships `minor` in the launch window). The note carries the BREAKING banner, both FROM → TO lines and the `adr-0087: registered` marker for the entry in scope.
- `@objectstack/setup` and `@objectstack/studio` are moved only in tests, a `test` script and `tsconfig.json`; both pack `dist` alone. No changeset entry is owed. The level axis of `Check Changeset` reads the same on this head.
- **`Check Changeset` is red for one reason, the DELIBERATE CORRECTION, and the correction is confirmed.** The job log's only error is the refusal to change `.changeset/36029-book-audience-system-permission.md`; its level, lockstep, empty-frontmatter and ADR-0087 steps pass. The diff of that file is one sentence.
  - Before: "It is strict, so `{ systemPermission, label }` is refused at parse; an object that also carries `permissionSet` still parses as the older, non-strict `{ permissionSet }` arm with the other key dropped, as before."
  - After: "It is strict, so `{ systemPermission, label }` is refused at parse, and an object that also carries `permissionSet` is refused too: an audience names one gate."
  - First clause, unchanged and still true: the arm is `strictObject`, so `{ systemPermission, label }` is refused. Second clause before: false on this head, since the set arm now refuses `systemPermission` and no arm accepts the pair. Second clause after: true on this head, in both key orders, and pinned by `book.test.ts`. Both notes are pending and release together, so the corrected sentence describes what ships. No other sentence of that note is changed, and none of the others is made false by this diff.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Route (schema, not lint) and the widened file surface:** answered by amendment 7214987476; the reason holds in the tree, since `defineStack` parses a book before any rule runs and the set arm stripped the key.
- **Leave the `{ permissionSet }` arm non-strict:** right. Stored book rows are kept as written, the card allows the strict arm only "if a stored book with a stray key is shown not to exist", and nothing shows that. The narrow form refuses exactly the pair the card names.
- **Test Core (4/10):** one driver-sql time-zone test timed out, the shard is green on re-run, and the diff touches no driver. Not this PR's.
- **A `public` book claiming by `include: '*'`** (the dev's unfiled note): not a finding on this PR. The card and the ADR-0046 §6.7 rule name gated books only, and this is the opposite direction of the same mechanism, which needs its own decision. It is security-touching: it goes on a separate card, and its particulars go to the seat privately.
- **SQL push-down:** no data access in the diff; nothing to push down.
- No `open_questions` entry is left on the card or the PR.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/system/book.zod.ts`**, against the card, ADR-0046 §6.7 and its first consumers (`audienceAllows`, the Setup and Studio manuals). The refused shape is exactly the two-gate audience, and the refusal is where every authoring door meets it. The message says which key means what and to delete the other; the strict arm's `history` says the pair used to gate on the set alone, which is what an author needs to choose. `guidance: { permissionSet }` on the strict arm names a key that arm does not declare, as the table requires. `z.never().optional()` rather than `retiredKey` is right: the key is not retired, and `retiredKey` would print a retirement sentence. The jsdoc sentences hold against the code: "only the second gate key is refused", "`audienceAllows` reads one of them", "a `defineStack` config is parsed before any rule runs". The shipped manuals (`{ systemPermission }`, `setup_*` / `studio_*`) parse unchanged.

**`19.book-audience-two-gates-and-catch-all-claim-refused.ts`**, against `SemanticMigration` in `migrations/types.ts` and its peers. It tells an author what to do: `replacement` names both forms with what each admits and the three ways to claim by name; `reason` says what the pair meant until now (the set alone) and that stored books are refused at the next save, not at boot; `acceptanceCriteria` is checkable. No D2 conversion is right, since which gate and which pages are the author's choice. One entry for two refusals of the same gate is acceptable beside the single changeset marker.

**`packages/lint/src/validate-book-audience-claims.ts`, `authoring-rules.ts`, `index.ts`**, against the ADR sentence ("never by `include: '*'`") and `matchesInclude`. The rule reads the book alone, names the book, the group and the path, and passes namespace globs, tag includes and pinned `pages`, as the ADR says. `gateOf` reads the two forms the way `audienceAllows` does. Registration (`gating`, `parsed`, all commands, `runtimeTypes: ['book']`) agrees with the docs row and the changeset. It reads `stack.books` as the sibling rule `validateCapabilityReferences` does.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

- N1 (nit) — the entry's comment gives as its reason for no relevance question that the runtime save door also judges books "which no question over one stack can name". `migrations/types.ts` says a relevance proof is about the definition the chain reads and that runtime-stored metadata is not part of it, and the surface lives only under `books`. Omitting `relevantWhen` is the permitted, always-listed default, so the result is correct; the entry is listed to upgraders who declare no book. Left as an accepted deviation.
- N2 (nit) — the rule's jsdoc calls `'*'` and `'**'` "the spellings that match every doc name". `globToRegExp` leaves `?` unescaped, so `'*?'` also matches every name and is not flagged; and the rule trims the glob where the matcher does not. The rule holds the ADR sentence as written, and a rule of this kind catches the mistake, not every spelling. Left as an accepted deviation, or one line on a follow-up card.

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`

MERGE-ONLY DELTA on record 7215110573 (PASS at `b999885037f1`). This record judges the merge commit `dc85e540` and what `main` brought under the PR; everything 7215110573 judged stands as written there and is not re-judged. Read: the merge commit and its combined diff, the net diff of the PR at both heads, the 19 commits of `main` the merge brings in (and the 6 `main` has added since), the rule registry at five commits, and the check-runs and two job logs on this head.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The merge brings only `main`, right.** `dc85e540` has parents `b999885037f1` (the head 7215110573 reviewed) and `c42a0454a706`. The second parent is an ancestor of `main` (6 commits behind today's tip `0a3ea67c2c02`). The five PR commits are unchanged (`git range-diff` reads `=` on all five).
